params.why: a zero step would put A and B at the same x-coordinate, giving a vertical line with no defined gradient

solution: Let the coordinates of $A$ be $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ and the coordinates of $B$ be $\left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$
Write down the formula for gradient: $m=\dfrac{y_{2}-y_{1}}{x_{2}-x_{1}}$
Write the final answer: the coordinates of $B$ are $\left({=x2}, {=y2}\right)$. Therefore $x={=x2}$.
notes: Entry-point version of the skill: one point fully known, gradient a positive whole number, the other point's y-coordinate known and x-coordinate the unknown to isolate — a direct single rearrangement of m=(y2-y1)/(x2-x1), same method as we04 (page 295) but generalised off H(x,0) to any known y2 so the family isn't stuck at y=0. Built from we04, whose figure (a segment from G(7,-9) to H(x,0) with mGH=3) I viewed to confirm the point/variable layout; this family drops the diagram and states both points as plain coordinates. Reviewer: check that m staying positive and small keeps this genuinely 'basic' relative to the advanced sibling family, and that t's sign is free (so B can sit left or right of A) without ever making x2==x1. Relevant catalogued errors a student could still make here even though there's no coefficient trick: mc:g10m8s3-1-2:mismatched-point-order and mc:g10m8s3-1-2:inverted-gradient-ratio (both apply to the plain gradient formula, not just to this family).
